description.narrative: The development objective of Adaptive Safety Net Project is to strengthen the social protection system in Senegal. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Strengthening the Core Delivery Systems for Social Protection, has the following sub-components: (i) Update, extension and quality enhancement of the National Social Registry (RNU); (ii) Decentralized delivery of frontline services; and (iii) Payment system and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM). 2) The second component, Promoting equity, resilience and productive inclusion, has the following sub-components: (i) Accompanying measures on human capital and productive inclusion for National Cash Transfer Program (PNBSF) beneficiaries; (ii) Productive inclusion program - Yokk Koom Koom; and (iii) Agricultural Resilience Program. 3) The third component, Providing shock-responsive assistance, has the following sub-components: (i) Delivering assistance in response to covariate shock; and (ii) Contingency Emergency Response. 4) The fourth component, Institutional support, project management and evaluation, has the following sub-components: (i) Institutional support and capacity building; and (ii) Project management and evaluation.
The objective of the project is to strengthen the social protection system in Senegal.

title.narrative: Programs with MIS interoperable with the RNU
Programs with MIS interoperable with the RNU

comment.narrative: The DGPSN payment platform is not integrated into the SIG. As part of the response to food insecurity, coordination is established between FSN, DGPSN and SECNSA and UNDP. The FSN, DGPSN and the Ministry of the Interior are also coordinating the response to flooding.

The identification and selection of beneficiaries for ASP programs are based on the RNU. The RNU data is available and updated through surveys. There are data-sharing protocols in place. Some government ASP programs have interoperable MIS with the RNU MIS. Beneficiary lists are shared with payment operators, who track payments and then send follow-up reports. A complaint management system exists. Both beneficiaries and non-beneficiaries can submit complaints, but not all complaints are addressed, and they may be handled with delays. Decentralized agents of the Ministry are responsible for coordinating and supervising ASP program activities in most regions of the country. The mechanisms for coordination, monitoring, sharing, and reporting information among the various actors are defined, but their implementation is imperfect. The Ministry's ASP programs are coordinated, but the coordination is limited to the DGPSN and FSN programs.
Since there were no PNBSF payments made over the past year (which continue to be paid in cash via the post offices) and all other payments are digital, this indicator amounts to 100%.

title.narrative: Households benefiting from productive support programs

comment.narrative: In FY23, productive inclusion activities of the Yokk Koom Koom program were scaled up to an additional 46,000 households. Activities started in October 2022 and cash transfers are implementing from October 2023, with households completing the program by early February 2024 instead to December 2023 as planned. With this new IDA project, PAPSA, an additional 80,000 new households will be supported over the duration of the project. In addition, after a pilot in FY22 (may-September 2021) which supported 10,500 households, the government plans to expand the Agricultural Resilience Program to 25,000 households in FY24 (starting in July 2023).
